ledger.failureMode: resolveEvidenceDir defaults the screenshot folder to a fixed, predictable path (os.tmpdir() joined with e2e-evidence), and the EvidenceCapture C# helper that renderEvidenceHelper writes into the E2E project defaults to Path.GetTempPath() joined with e2e-evidence; the folder is created with default permissions and the screenshot is written through PageScreenshotOptions.Path with no ownership, mode or symlink check, so on a host whose temp directory is shared (Linux /tmp) the end-state screenshots of the QA application are readable by other local users, and another user can pre-create that folder or plant an AC-id.png symlink there to read the files or redirect the write.
ledger.evidence: Read packages/e2e-testing/lib/evidence-capture.js (read-only inspection, nothing executed): resolveEvidenceDir (lines 46-49) returns path.resolve(E2E_EVIDENCE_DIR, or path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'e2e-evidence') when unset). The command text (Phase 2 step 4 of author-playwright-tests) carries that value to every Run request as evidenceDir, and the agent exports it as E2E_EVIDENCE_DIR for the test run. The helper source in renderEvidenceHelper (lines 98-121) calls Directory.CreateDirectory on that folder and then _page.ScreenshotAsync with PageScreenshotOptions Path = <folder>/<acId>.png, with no check of who owns the folder, no restrictive mode, and no refusal of an existing folder or symlink; the file name is predictable from the AC id. os.tmpdir() is per-user on macOS and Windows but /tmp on Linux. evidence-capture.js has no hunk in any slice of this change, so these lines predate it. Direction: default to a per-user folder created with mode 0700 (for example fs.mkdtempSync under os.tmpdir(), or a folder under the user's home), or refuse an evidence folder the current user does not own.

ledger.failureMode: detectE2eFramework treats any package id that merely starts with nunit or xunit as the project's test framework, so an xUnit project that also references the framework-neutral NunitXml.TestLogger package is classified as ambiguous (null) and the command then falls back to NUnit, scaffolding NUnit attributes into an xUnit project (or refusing to append to its existing xUnit class with a framework mismatch error).
ledger.evidence: Read e2e-framework.js:24-25 (name.startsWith('nunit') / name.startsWith('xunit') on the lower-cased Include value). Ran a throwaway node script against the snapshot's lib: detectE2eFramework of a csproj referencing xunit, xunit.runner.visualstudio, Microsoft.Playwright and NunitXml.TestLogger printed null (xunit plus Microsoft.Playwright alone printed xunit; a single-quoted Include='xunit' also printed null because PACKAGE_RE only accepts double quotes). NunitXml.TestLogger is the spekt VSTest logger package, usable with any test framework, so it says nothing about which framework the E2E project uses. author-playwright-tests.yaml:151 then carries framework 'nunit' when the result is null, so scaffoldNewSpecFile is asked for NUnit output for a new spec; and appendTestMethod(existing xUnit class, framework 'nunit') printed: framework mismatch: the existing file uses xunit but framework 'nunit' was requested, whereas the same call with framework omitted inferred [Fact] (printed true). So both the heuristic and the explicit-nunit fallback defeat the file-based inference the writer already has. The new tests (e2e-framework.test.js) have no case with a logger or other non-framework nunit*/xunit* package.

ledger.evidence: Read, not run. spec-writer.js:240-244 emits 'private readonly <fixtureType> _fixture;', a constructor parameter 'fixture' and '_fixture = fixture;', and renderTestMethodBlock splices the caller's testBody in verbatim. author-playwright-tests.yaml:226 says a new xunit file needs only {collection, fixtureType} copied from a sibling spec class; playwright-tester.yaml:61 tells the author to 'build the context and page as the project's sibling tests do'; a grep of both files for _fixture finds nothing, so the name is an unstated coupling. ledger.failureMode: detectE2eFramework maps a project that references Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit to 'xunit', but Playwright's own xUnit package ships a PageTest base class with a Page property, so such projects have no [Collection] class and no injected fixture. Everything downstream of the 'xunit' label assumes the other shape: scaffoldNewSpecFile throws for a new xunit file unless the caller supplies a collection name and a fixture type (the message tells the caller to copy them from a sibling spec class, which does not exist in such a project); the playwright-tester agent text says 'framework xunit means no PageTest Page'; the ProposalRequest typedef says xUnit tests build their own page. scaffoldXunitFile checks only the spelling of collection and fixtureType, not that the fixture exists, so an agent that invents a pair gets a class that cannot compile. Appending a [Fact] to an existing PageTest-based file works, so what breaks is landing a new file and the authoring guidance. No test covers this shape: e2e-framework.test.js only asserts that the package name counts as xunit, and spec-writer-xunit.test.js only builds the [Collection]-fixture shape.
ledger.evidence: Read e2e-framework.js:25 (name === 'microsoft.playwright.xunit' sets the xunit flag) and e2e-framework.test.js:30 (Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit listed under 'counts as xunit'); spec-writer.js:213-223 (comment 'xUnit has no base class to inherit a page from'; collection and fixtureType are required); agents/playwright-tester.yaml:61 ('framework 'xunit' means no PageTest `Page`'); delegation-contract.js:50-52.
